Injective: Voting opens on Veyra Mainnet Upgrade proposal - 12 Nov 2026 Less than 1 min read

INJUSD Injective opens voting on the Veyra Mainnet Upgrade proposal on 12 Nov 2026. The proposal covers infrastructure for institutional use of real-world assets (RWAs), expanded enterprise gateways and groundwork for native privacy through CypherOS. A passing vote would advance the proposed protocol expansion for INJ. Approval would move the proposal through governance, but the upgrade itself would still be pending activation. Voting does not activate the proposed changes.

The Injective Veyra Mainnet Upgrade is now live for voting. Our final major upgrade of 2026 introduces new institutional RWA infrastructure, expanded enterprise gateways, and lays the foundation for native privacy with CypherOS. The new age of finance will be on $INJ pic.twitter.com/8rVbKq5Y0c

News / London Stock Exchange / REG - KR1 PLC - Update: Venice Infrastructure Operations

REG - KR1 PLC - Update: Venice Infrastructure Operations Refinitiv 3 min read

KR1 RNS Number : 7982C KR1 PLC 12 November 2026   KR1 plc Thursday, 12 November 2026 KR1 plc (“KR1” or the “Company”) Update: Venice Infrastructure Operations KR1 plc KR1 , a London Stock Exchange-listed onchain infrastructure company, is pleased to provide an update on its Venice (“VVV”) operations. Following its October Infrastructure Income & Holdings update, in which it reported holding 276,223 VVV valued at £5.77 million as at 30 September 2026, the Company has fully staked its current holding of 275,000 VVV, earning rewards in VVV at an indicative annualised staking rate of approximately 5.74% as at 11 November 2026. Based on available disclosures, the Company believes it is the largest publicly listed holder of VVV, with approximately 0.56% of the circulating supply, a position that reflects its conviction in the convergence of AI and crypto. Venice is a core holding within KR1’s Technology Infrastructure Strategy. In its Introducing Decentralised AI announcement on 14 May 2026, the Company disclosed an initial holding of 60,000 VVV and the commencement of staking operations. KR1 has since increased its position. Founded by renowned crypto entrepreneur Erik Voorhees, Venice provides access to frontier and open-source AI models for generating text, code, images, video and audio. The platform is designed around privacy, model choice and user control. Venice’s adoption continues to accelerate. Its October community update reported 5 million users, with the increase from 4 million taking 68 days. Daily inference volume exceeded one trillion tokens during October, compared with approximately 250 billion at the end of September. On 14 October, Venice’s Erik Voorhees reported annual revenue exceeding US$150 million. In July, Venice also announced a US$65 million Series A led by Dragonfly, at a stated US$1 billion valuation, to expand its consumer platform and API business. KR1 puts its Venice assets to productive use in two ways. First, the Company stakes VVV to generate infrastructure income in the form of newly issued VVV tokens. Reward rates vary, and standard VVV unstaking is subject to a seven-day cooldown. The second route uses DIEM, a token that holders can mint by locking staked VVV. KR1 acquired its DIEM separately and stakes it to access daily credits for AI inference on Venice. KR1 makes that inference capacity available to customers through third-party marketplaces. Venice’s buy-and-burn programme creates a further connection between commercial adoption and VVV. The platform allocates 5% of API credit purchases to buying VVV on the open market and permanently removing it from supply. New Pro, Pro+ and Max subscriptions trigger purchases and burns of US$2, US$5 and US$10, respectively, alongside discretionary burns. Venice reported that the value of VVV burned during October had exceeded US$1 million by 28 October. Revenue-funded purchases create demand for VVV, while burns reduce VVV supply relative to continuing issuance. This mechanism is separate from staking rewards and does not constitute a cash distribution to token holders. Keld van Schreven, Managing Director and Co-Founder of KR1 plc, commented: “We believe the convergence of AI and crypto could be one of the defining technology themes of the next decade. We put that conviction to work through our Venice operations, staking VVV to earn infrastructure income while retaining exposure to the platform’s growth. We can use those rewards to fund operations or reinvest them in productive assets. That reinvestment drives the KR1 flywheel, helping grow the earning capacity behind each KR1 equity share.” About KR1 plc KR1 plc owns and operates productive digital assets across the networks powering the convergence of AI and crypto. As the only dedicated onchain infrastructure company listed on the Main Market of the London Stock Exchange, KR1 draws on a decade of domain expertise to take a high-conviction, thesis-driven approach to its holdings, targeting a dual return profile: infrastructure income and capital appreciation. News / ACCESS Newswire / Elektros Schedules Preliminary Florida Meeting to Discuss Potential Acquisition of Its Multi-Port EV Charging Patent

Elektros Schedules Preliminary Florida Meeting to Discuss Potential Acquisition of Its Multi-Port EV Charging Patent 4 min read

ELEK Company says prospective interested party may explore acquiring some or all rights to U.S. Patent No. 12,522,100 B1; no terms or agreement have been reached. WEST PALM BEACH, FL / ACCESS Newswire / November 11, 2026 / Preliminary Meeting Scheduled for November 12 ELEKTROS Inc. ELEK , a publicly traded company, today announced that it expects to hold a preliminary meeting on Thursday, November 12, 2026, at 11:00 a.m. Eastern Time, at an undisclosed location in Florida not far from West Palm Beach. The meeting is expected to involve representatives of a prospective interested party and will focus on whether that party may wish to acquire the company's rights to its patented multi-port electric-vehicle charging technology. The contemplated discussion is an initial meeting of the minds only. ELEKTROS intends to use the meeting to understand the prospective party's objectives and to discuss whether a potential transaction involving the patent could make strategic and commercial sense. The identity of the prospective party and the meeting location are not being disclosed at this preliminary stage. Potential Patent Transaction Remains Exploratory The discussions are preliminary and exploratory. The parties may consider a potential purchase or other transfer of some or all rights associated with the patent, potentially including a full assignment of the patent rights to the prospective counterparty. No price, valuation, transaction structure, exclusivity, definitive agreement, or closing timetable has been agreed. The meeting is not a signed transaction, commitment, offer, or assurance that a transaction will occur. Any potential transaction would be subject to due diligence, negotiation, required approvals, definitive written documentation, and other customary conditions. The Patented Multi-Port Charging Architecture The technology is covered by U.S. Patent No. 12,522,100 B1, titled "Multi-Port Charging Assembly for Electric Vehicles," issued January 13, 2026. As described in the patent, the architecture brings multiple power inputs together and uses electronic control to assess supply and vehicle requirements, balance inputs, and provide adjusted output to an electric vehicle. The patent record identifies the invention as a multi-port charging assembly; the existence of the patent does not establish any particular charging speed or commercial performance. A Market Focused on Charging Speed Why high-speed charging matters: Reuters reported on April 24, 2026, that BYD was making ultra-fast charging central to its effort to address driver concerns about long charging times and range anxiety. Reuters quoted BYD Executive Vice President Stella Li describing flash charging as important because it "solves the last barrier for EV adoption." Bloomberg reported on January 28, 2026, that long refueling times had been a "stumbling block to EV adoption," while U.S. networks added approximately 11,300 ultra-fast charging cords in 2025, a 48% increase from 2024, according to data cited in the report. These third-party reports describe broader industry developments and do not validate ELEKTROS' technology or imply any relationship, endorsement, or transaction involving ELEKTROS. ELEKTROS believes that multi-input charging architectures could contribute to a paradigm shift in the high-speed EV charging sector if engineering, safety, compatibility, and commercial requirements can be successfully addressed. That is the company's view of the technology's potential-not a claim that a paradigm shift has occurred or that the patented system has achieved a verified charging result. The company has previously described an aspirational objective of approximately six to seven minutes for a full recharge; that objective has not been demonstrated or independently verified and is not being represented as an available product capability. CEO Commentary "We believe this patent merits serious, thoughtful evaluation because charging speed and convenience remain important issues for the electric-vehicle market," said Shlomo Bleier, Chief Executive Officer of ELEKTROS Inc. "Tomorrow's meeting is preliminary. Our focus is to understand the prospective party's interest, review possible structures, and determine whether there is a basis for further discussions. No agreement has been reached." About ELEKTROS Inc. About ELEKTROS Inc.: ELEKTROS Inc. ELEK is a publicly traded company whose areas of interest include electric-vehicle charging infrastructure, patented multi-port EV charging technology, and hard-rock lithium opportunities. Disclaimer Forward-Looking Statements and Important Risk Disclosure Forward-Looking Statements and Important Risk Disclosure: This release contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of applicable securities laws, including statements about the anticipated meeting, potential interest in the patent, possible negotiations, a potential sale or assignment of patent rights, and the potential applications or performance of the technology. The meeting may be postponed, changed, or may not occur, and discussions may end without an agreement. There can be no assurance that any party will make an offer, that terms will be agreed, that a transaction will be approved or completed, or that the technology can be engineered, tested, certified, commercialized, or achieve any particular charging speed. Actual results may differ materially due to technical and engineering challenges, battery and vehicle compatibility, electrical and thermal safety, regulatory requirements, intellectual-property matters, financing, counterparties, competition, market acceptance, and other risks. The patent itself does not prove commercial feasibility or a specific charging-time outcome. ELEK is a speculative microcap security, and investors could lose some or all of their invested capital. This release is for informational purposes only and is not an offer to sell or a solicitation to buy securities. Readers should conduct their own due diligence and consult their financial, legal, and tax advisers. Industry reporting referenced: Reuters, "BYD doubles down on fast charging to target China's EV holdouts," April 24, 2026 ( reuters.com ); Bloomberg, "Charging Companies Bet US Drivers Want More Ultra-Fast Stations," January 28, 2026 ( bloomberg.com ). Patent record: U.S. Patent No. 12,522,100 B1; USPTO Patent Center, Application No. 18/049,373. SOURCE: Elektros, Inc.

item.title: Asian markets mixed as Nvidia shares tumble; South Korea, Taiwan stocks slip
item.description: In the chip supply chain, SK Hynix slid, while Samsung Electronics surrendered part of its early gains. Traders also seemed to be watching Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (TSMC) closely, since ...
item.content:encoded:
News / CNBC TV18 /

Asian markets mixed as Nvidia shares tumble; South Korea, Taiwan stocks slip NVDA NI225 KOSPI IX0001 Asian markets opened mixed on Thursday November 12, with little conviction as investors seemed to weigh the fresh turmoil at Nvidia, the chipmaker at the centre of this year's artificial intelligence rally. Japan's Topix gained 0.51% and the Nikkei 225 added 0.17%. South Korea's Kospi slipped 0.068%, and Taiwan's TAIEX lost 0.24%, while Hang Seng futures dropped 0.7%. In the chip supply chain, SK Hynix slid, while Samsung Electronics surrendered part of its early gains. Traders also seemed to be watching Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (TSMC) closely, since any lasting damage to confidence in Nvidia could hit its key suppliers hardest. In India, the GIFT Nifty pointed to a muted start for the domestic market, though with a positive bias. The Nifty and the Nifty Bank both showed their first signs of exhaustion at higher levels after several sessions of strong gains, which suggested that the market could enter a phase of consolidation before it resumes its uptrend. The Nifty Bank was particularly in focus for the day's trade having come within 400 points of its previous record high. Separately, MSCI announced the results of its November review early Thursday. It added four Indian stocks to its Global Standard Index: Life Insurance Corporation of India, Coforge, Adani Green Energy and Meesho. Currency market in Asia too remains in focus as Japan's top currency official, Atsushi Mimura, told reporters according to a Bloomberg report that the Japanese yen's recent slide had been "too fast", adding that "It's too early to forget what happened this summer." The yen hovered near 160 per dollar, the level at which Tokyo stepped in over the summer. The trigger for the movement in Asian equities today, came in late US trading as Nvidia shares tumbled about 9% after Bloomberg reported that the company's board was meeting to discuss the future of Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang. Bloomberg said Huang had admitted to an affair with a woman whom US officials reportedly suspect of being a Chinese spy. The New York Times separately reported that Huang had a relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's healthcare vice president, citing several current and former employees. The shock cut short a strong day for US technology stocks, when the Nasdaq 100 had climbed 2.3%. Futures reversed course afterwards as Nasdaq 100 contracts fell more than 1%, and S&P 500 contracts lost 0.5%. Server makers Super Micro Computer and Dell Technologies also declined. Advanced Micro Devices and Broadcom rose as traders seemed to have speculated that they could pick up business if Nvidia stumbled. CoreWeave had surged 25% on an upbeat outlook before giving back some of that gain. In energy markets, Brent crude remained steady at about $92.46 a barrel in early Asia trade, after two straight days of losses. A senior Iranian official rejected the idea of surrendering enriched uranium, which signalled that peace talks between Washington and Tehran remain stalled.
